items.title: Housing decree faces November 12 survival vote
items.body: Spain's standing parliamentary committee votes on November 12 on Royal Decree-law 29/2026, in force since October 6. Passage is expected by one vote. The consumer ministry estimates median savings of €4,341 per household if all eligible tenants request the two-year extension for contracts expiring before December 31, 2028.

items.title: Empty homes could face up to 150% property tax surcharge
items.body: Royal Decree-law 29/2026 allows councils to add up to 150% to IBI (local property tax) from 2027, depending on how long a home is empty and who owns it. Each council must set rules and prove a home is empty without justification. Second homes are exempt for up to four consecutive years. The decree faces a November 12 vote.

items.title: Housing strike ends with clashes and arrests
items.body: At least 100 people were arrested across Spain during the November 11 housing strike. Barcelona saw looting and burning barricades, while police charged protesters in Madrid. The Interior Ministry recorded 919 incidents, and pickets blocked major roads in both regions.

items.title: Sick-leave pay calculation changes from December 1
items.body: Royal Decree-law 31/2026 changes how sick pay is calculated for leave starting on or after December 1, 2026. Social Security will use the contribution base from two months earlier, rather than one. Rates stay at 0% for days 1–3, 60% for days 4–20, and 75% from day 21. Pay may rise or fall depending on each worker's contributions.

items.title: Judge extends Zapatero influence-peddling probe by six months
items.body: National Court judge José Luis Calama extended by six months the investigation into former prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero for alleged influence peddling. Investigators are examining whether his consultancy payments hid a €500,000 commission for Plus Ultra's €53 million rescue. Witness statements and police analysis are pending.

items.title: Sabadell fined €16.5 million over mortgage insurance
items.body: The Bank of Spain fined Sabadell €16.5 million for making mortgages conditional on buying insurance products between January 2022 and March 2023. The bank has appealed in court. Spanish law bans compulsory tied sales but allows bundles that benefit the customer.

items.title: Pyrenees conservation project wins €100,000 grant
items.body: The Kilian Jornet Foundation won a €100,000 Impact Grant from the ISPO Impact Foundation. It will fund three years of trail restoration and research in the Cerdanya area of the Pyrenees. The project will restore more than 15 kilometres of trails, build raised walkways over wetlands, and monitor vulnerable species.

items.title: Prosecutors open TikTok child abuse content investigation
items.body: Attorney General Teresa Peramato has ordered an investigation into child sexual abuse content on TikTok after a complaint from fact-checking outlet Maldita. Maldita reported more than 1,000 videos with over 48 million views. Spain's data protection agency will ask TikTok about its removal efforts before ordering a block on access.

items.title: PP proposes benefits tied to job searches
items.body: PP leader and prime ministerial candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo proposes merging the minimum-income benefit and subsidies into an "activation income" compatible with work. Recipients would sign training and job-search agreements. Repeated refusal of suitable jobs without justification would gradually cut aid. This is an election proposal.

items.title: Energy support offers electricity discounts and heating payments
items.body: Spain's electricity social bonus remains in force, offering eligible households discounts of 42.5% or 57.5% within consumption limits. It requires a regulated PVPC tariff and contracted power of 10 kW or less. Households holding it on December 31 automatically qualify for the following year's heating payment of €50–€373.
